name: Instant-Colossus
geological_features: Rapidly forming and dissolving storm systems
Pressure-crushed diamond rain in deep atmosphere
specific_features: Atmospheric changes that normally take centuries occur in hours
description: Instant-Colossus is the largest gas giant in its system and one of the most dynamic ever catalogued. Storm systems that would persist for decades on comparable worlds form and dissolve in mere hours here, their life cycles compressed as if the planet exists on an accelerated timescale.

The toxic atmosphere is a churning chaos of hydrogen, helium, and exotic compounds, lit from within by lightning superstorms that discharge enough energy to power a civilization. Diamond rain falls through the deeper layers, crushed from carbon by pressures that defy easy comprehension.

The accelerated atmospheric dynamics have no accepted explanation. Some theorists propose the planet's core rotates at a different rate than its outer layers, creating shear forces that compress weather patterns. Others note that trace antimatter signatures in the upper atmosphere suggest processes occurring here that physics models do not fully account for.

The antimatter traces make Instant-Colossus one of the most valuable bodies in the sector, as even trace harvesting yields quantities worth fortunes. The unpredictable atmospheric dynamics make collection operations hazardous, with weather windows measured in minutes rather than days.
